description: This account holds that achieving automaticity in low-level transcription skills frees attentional resources for higher-level processes.

description: The article draws on McLaughlin's (1987) cognitive theory and information processing models, in which learning a complex cognitive skill requires the automatization of component subskills.
title: Automaticity theory: automatizing component subskills frees controlled processing for higher-order functions such as comprehension

description: Automaticity Theory (AT) is presented as a main theory in developing reading fluency, emphasizing word recognition.
title: Automaticity Theory: fluency develops through repeated practice that frees attention for comprehension

description: The article proposes that the emotionally engendered by words affects retention through autonomic rather than cortical arousal.
title: Autonomic (rather than cortical) arousal account of the word-arousal memory effect
